labels.title: Perfboard
labels.description: The soldered perfboard connects the Arduino, sensors, and logging modules through removable headers. It replaced the prototype breadboard, but the tight wiring clearance made assembly and troubleshooting difficult. A future version would combine the electronics on a single PCB.

labels.title: Wheel-speed sensor mount
labels.description: This mount positions an A3144 Hall-effect sensor near the wheel hub. Two magnets in each hub were intended to trigger the sensor as the wheel turned, allowing the Arduino to calculate wheel speed. The sensors worked on the breadboard but failed in the installed circuit. This CAD export includes the mount; the sensor and magnets are not modeled as separate parts.

labels.title: Front suspension
labels.description: Printed control arms and knuckles form the front double-wishbone suspension. Caster and kingpin inclination help the wheels self-center. The knuckles were the main failure point during impacts.

labels.title: Aerodynamics
labels.description: The wings and floor were designed to fit the completed chassis. Their shapes were limited by printing and packaging constraints, and aerodynamic performance was not validated with CFD.

labels.title: Rear drivetrain
labels.description: The motor drives a differential and CV axles at the rear wheels. This arrangement lets the wheels turn at different speeds through a corner.

labels.title: Brushless motor
labels.description: A DYS D3542 brushless outrunner powers the car from a 14.8 V battery. Its 1450 KV rating describes no-load speed per volt; it does not predict the car’s speed under load. Ground testing reached about 30 mph.

labels.title: LiPo battery
labels.description: The 14.8 V LiPo powers the motor through the speed controller. A 5 V supply serves the electronics, and a separate UBEC supplies 7 V to the steering servo.

labels.title: Arduino Nano
labels.description: The Arduino Nano processes radio commands, controls throttle and steering, and collects data for logging. It replaced the larger Uno used during prototyping.

labels.title: Steering servo
labels.description: The servo moves the front wheels through the steering linkage. The suspension geometry helps the wheels return to center, improving straight-line stability despite play in the printed joints.

labels.title: Speed controller
labels.description: The FlyColor 50 A electronic speed controller regulates motor power. It was designed for drones and did not provide regenerative braking in this build.

labels.title: IMU
labels.description: The MPU6050 measures acceleration and orientation during test runs. Those readings are recorded alongside the driver’s control inputs.

labels.title: SD data logger
labels.description: A microSD module stores the test logs. A startup counter in the Arduino’s EEPROM gives each run a separate CSV filename.

labels.title: Front wing
labels.description: The front wing was intended to generate downforce and redirect air around the front tires. It broke during testing before its aerodynamic performance could be properly evaluated.

labels.title: Rear wing
labels.description: The rear wing was designed for downforce, with a relatively simple shape that could be printed. Its contribution was not measured separately.

labels.title: Floor / underbody
labels.description: Two Venturi tunnels and side skirts form the underbody design. The flat chassis and limited ride height restricted the tunnel geometry. Select this label to view the underside.

labels.title: Rear diffuser
labels.description: The diffuser expands the underbody flow path at the rear of the floor. Its geometry had to fit around the chassis and drivetrain; its aerodynamic effect was not measured separately.

labels.title: Rear suspension
labels.description: The rear double wishbones use anti-squat geometry to reduce ride-height changes under acceleration. The geometry still allows some squat and suspension travel over bumps.

labels.title: Sidepods
labels.description: These printed body panels enclose components beside the chassis. Their shape follows the mechanical layout established earlier in the build.

labels.title: Differential
labels.description: The differential lets the driven rear wheels turn at different speeds in a corner. It is supported by ball bearings inside the rear suspension mount.

labels.title: Cooling fan
labels.description: Printed mounts position the fan near the motor. The Cooling view makes the surrounding ducting translucent so both components are visible.

labels.title: Printed fan mounts
labels.description: Printed brackets hold the cooling fan beside the motor.

labels.title: Motor ducting
labels.description: Printed ducting surrounds the motor area. It becomes translucent in the Cooling view to reveal the components inside.

labels.title: Drive input shaft
labels.description: A short 4 mm hex shaft and 5 mm coupler connect the motor to the differential. The coupler relies on friction against the smooth motor shaft; stripped screws caused repeated replacement.

labels.title: Halfshafts / CV axles
labels.description: The paired shafts carry torque from the differential to the rear hubs. Their articulated joints accommodate the movement of the rear suspension.

labels.title: Rear wheel hubs
labels.description: The driven hubs connect the halfshafts to the rear wheels. The wheels are hidden in this view to expose the hub geometry.

labels.title: Wheel-speed magnet pockets
labels.description: The cutouts in the printed wheel hub locate the two wheel-speed magnets. The Hall-effect sensor reads their passage. Select this label to look at the exposed hub; the magnets themselves are not separate parts in this export.

labels.title: Left sidepod intake
labels.description: The front opening of the left sidepod admits air into the body and the motor cooling path. The marker sits at the inlet mouth, ahead of the internal scoop.

labels.title: Right sidepod intake
labels.description: The front opening of the right sidepod admits air into the body and the motor cooling path. The marker sits at the inlet mouth, ahead of the internal scoop.

labels.title: Top air intake
labels.description: The forward-facing opening in the raised top cover provides another air path into the body. The marker sits in the opening instead of on the rear of the cover. Its contribution to cooling was not measured separately.

labels.title: Shark fin
labels.description: The thin vertical fin runs along the top cover ahead of the rear wing. It is part of the cover in this CAD assembly.

labels.title: Bargeboards
labels.description: The bargeboards sit ahead of the sidepods. The helical guides illustrate possible rolled-up edge flow moving downstream; they are a visualization of the design intent, not CFD results.

labels.title: Floor leading edge / edge vortices
labels.description: The front of the floor and its outer edges are shown with illustrative vortex paths. The actual flow structure and its strength would require simulation or flow testing.

labels.title: Ackermann
labels.description: The front wheels steer through different angles to follow their respective turning radii. Front wheel-angle readouts include 2.07° of static toe per wheel. Rear headings follow the fixed rear hub orientations. Drag the steering wheel to rotate the central steering mechanism. The tie rods keep their length and turn the knuckles about their ball joints. The animation uses joint positions from the CAD.

labels.title: Caster
labels.description: Caster is the steering-axis tilt in side view. The gold axis passes through the front knuckle’s upper and lower ball joints. The outboard projection compares its fore–aft tilt with the dashed vertical reference. Rear guides show the corresponding upright joint-axis tilt; the rear wheels do not steer.

labels.title: Kingpin Inclination
labels.description: KPI is the steering-axis tilt in front view. The gold line joins the upper and lower knuckle joints; its front-view projection shows the inward tilt against vertical. This is a different axis from the wheel’s camber. Rear guides show the corresponding upright joint-axis tilt; the rear wheels do not steer.

labels.title: Camber
labels.description: Camber is the wheel plane’s tilt from vertical in front view. The gold ring follows the wheel plane derived from the CAD hub face. The reference lines compare that plane with vertical; the angle is projected from the exported CAD pose. Both front and rear wheel planes are shown.

labels.title: Toe
labels.description: Toe is the wheel’s heading relative to the car’s centerline in top view. Toe-out is positive; toe-in is negative. Static toe is set to +2.07° per wheel. Gold arrows show the wheel headings above the front axle; dashed white lines point straight ahead. Rear readouts follow the fixed rear hub orientations.

labels.title: Rear anti-squat
labels.description: Rear anti-squat comes from the side-view suspension geometry. Gold marks the inboard pickup directions and their projections through the outboard joints; white marks the ground reference and the contact-patch line to the projected instant center. Pickup centers are approximated from the exported mesh. A percentage would also require the center of mass and drive-force assumptions, so none is shown.
